text.p: French first division matches this weekend (standings in brackets, all kickoff times GMT):

The first division leaders, at full strength, should beat lowly Nancy at home to ensure they cannot be caught by Monaco, who play on Saturday and are now one point behind. Nancy scored their first goal in four games in 1-1 draw against Lens last week.
Nantes, who made awful start to season, will go record 14 matches unbeaten if they avoid defeat at Lens, who have slumped after best start of four successive wins.
UEFA Cup quarter-finalists Monaco will want to keep pressure on leaders PSG by winning this home match, but Guingamp, 2-1 winners against Bastia on Friday and unbeaen in four games, will not be easy.
The champions must quickly come down to earth from their European Cup exploits if they are going to resist the formidable challenge of in-form Bordeaux.

The Corsicans, whose four-match winning streak was ended at Guingamp last Friday, will be looking to bounce back against bottom club Nice, who are in middle of change in management and whose surprise 3-1 win over Rennes only eased tensions slightly.

Metz must overcome disappointment of UEFA Cup elimination by Newcastle United for visit of Marseille, who have had three 0-0 draws in last four games and have shown interest in signing Brazilian striker Oseas of Atletico Parana. Their midfielder Eric Roy is doubtful.
Strasbourg, who have surprised with their high placing, rely heavily on first division joint top scorer David Zitelli, who hit two more in 3-0 win over Lyon last week.
Home win would put Rennes level with Lille in tight middle sector of standings.
Caen's goal against PSG last week was their first in five games but defeat extended losing streak to five. Lyon, who have poor away record, are unbeaten at home.

Both sides will be looking for points to pull away from the four-team relegation zone. Cannes have one of the division's weakest attacks -- 13 goals in 20 games -- while Montpellier have not won in five matches.
